turns.en: But the tension shifted to AI credit very, very quickly. And the story turned to CoreWeave, where shares were down close to 16%, while the outstanding bond yields that they have were up to 15%, essentially going to junk status.
turns.zh: 但紧张情绪非常快就转移到了 AI 信贷。故事转向了 CoreWeave，股价下跌近16%，而他们未偿债券收益率上升到15%，基本上进入垃圾级状态。

turns.en: Now this is about a potential domino effect. So many people are asking, is CoreWeave that important that they can actually turn the markets?
turns.zh: 现在这是关于潜在的多米诺骨牌效应。所以很多人在问：CoreWeave 真的那么重要，以至于能扭转市场吗？

turns.en: Well, this is really about the fact that AI has been sucking up so much credit in order to create growth. And inevitably, the growth will start to potentially stall when their access to credit also slows.
turns.zh: 嗯，这实际上是因为 AI 一直在吸收这么多信贷来创造增长。不可避免地，当他们获得信贷的渠道也放缓时，增长将开始潜在地停滞。

turns.en: So the real question is, is CoreWeave that important? Well, really the whole market is just trying to figure out when is the financing cycle going to get stressed?
turns.zh: 所以真正的问题是：CoreWeave 真的那么重要吗？嗯，实际上整个市场只是在试图弄清楚融资周期什么时候会承压。

turns.en: When is the credit available to these AI stories going to start drying up and therefore slowing the growth story? And what yesterday really was was potentially the first kind of sign that that situation is developing.
turns.zh: 这些 AI 故事可获得的信贷什么时候会开始枯竭，从而放缓增长故事？昨天实际上可能是那种情况正在发展的第一个迹象。

turns.en: So what we really saw was a substantial decline in many of the NASDAQ-driven AI stories. And that's where all the selling came. And this was accompanied by very clear sector rotation, which I want to talk about.
turns.zh: 所以我们真正看到的是很多 NASDAQ 驱动的 AI 故事大幅下跌。所有的抛售都来自那里。这伴随着非常明显的板块轮动，我想谈谈这个。

turns.en: That's exactly what I want to talk about, Patrick, because for weeks we were pinned at the highs in markets. But really, what are you expecting to see here over the next few weeks and months?
turns.zh: 这正是我想谈的，Patrick，因为连续几周市场都被钉在高位。但真的，你预计未来几周和几个月会看到什么？

turns.en: Well, let's just start off by actually what potentially happened yesterday. We had a scenario over the last few weeks where their money was literally flowing into the NASDAQ and out of the rest of the market.
turns.zh: 嗯，让我们先从昨天可能发生了什么开始。过去几周我们有一个场景，钱简直是在流入 NASDAQ、流出市场的其他部分。

turns.en: And this was most evident in the Commitment of Trader reports, where we saw the positioning score on the NASDAQ in the 100th percentile, while the Russell's small caps were pretty much pinned towards the 0th percentile on the downside.
turns.zh: 这在 Commitment of Traders（交易者持仓）报告中最为明显，我们看到 NASDAQ 的持仓分数在第100百分位，而 Russell 小盘股几乎被钉在下行的第0百分位附近。

turns.en: That money flow was incredibly evident. Everyone was still piling in to this NASDAQ trade. But we clearly saw yesterday the start of some sort of sector rotation.
turns.zh: 那种资金流非常明显。每个人还在涌入这个 NASDAQ 交易。但我们昨天清楚地看到了某种板块轮动的开始。

turns.en: Yesterday, all the defensives were ripping higher, including bonds. We had basically utilities, consumer staples, healthcare, all advancing, while we basically saw very strong pullbacks in almost all of the AI-driven names.
turns.zh: 昨天，所有的防御性板块都在飙升，包括债券。我们基本上有公用事业、必需消费品、医疗保健都在上涨，而基本上我们看到几乎所有 AI 驱动的股票都出现了非常强劲的回调。

turns.en: And so now one day doesn't make a new trend, but we can't ignore when something big like this starts to happen, because we have to determine whether or not this is the beginning of a new trend and a bigger sector rotation.
turns.zh: 所以现在一天不能造就一个新趋势，但当这么大的事情开始发生时，我们不能忽视，因为我们必须判断这是不是一个新趋势和更大板块轮动的开始。

turns.en: And that is definitely going to be the story in equities. Are we going to see those beaten up sectors that were pulling the breath of the market down over the last few weeks, suddenly have meaningful rebounds?
turns.zh: 而这肯定将是股票的故事。我们是否会看到那些过去几周把市场拖累下来的被打压的板块，突然有意义的反弹？

turns.en: And are we going to see some of the tripwires hit on some of the sell triggers on the NASDAQ and potentially the S&P 500, where some of these CTAs and systematic selling strategies are going to be forced to deleverage their long positioning?
turns.zh: 我们是否会看到 NASDAQ 甚至 S&P 500 上的一些卖出触发器的绊线（tripwires）被触发，一些 CTA 和系统性卖出策略将被迫去杠杆他们的多头头寸？

turns.en: It's going to be certainly a very interesting next few weeks. Well, let's turn to treasuries, because we've seen volatility coming in here too.
turns.zh: 这肯定将是非常有趣的几周。好，让我们转向国债，因为我们看到这里的波动率也在上升。

turns.en: But do you believe investors could be buying back in as they seek protection now, especially with what we're seeing in equities? And if that's the case, do you think that's even sustainable?
turns.zh: 但你认为投资人现在可能在买回以寻求保护吗，尤其是看到股市的情况？如果是这样，你认为这甚至可持续吗？

turns.en: It's a great question, Maseel, but the one thing that I would want to actually focus on is actually the way the bond market behaved yesterday, because to me, that's the part that can't be ignored.
turns.zh: 这是个很好的问题，Michelle，但我真的想聚焦的是昨天债券市场的行为方式，因为对我来说，那是不能被忽视的部分。

turns.en: What we saw was a hot CPI number, bond yield started to rise, and by the end of the day, from peak to trough, we saw close to a 25 basis point move in both the 10-year and the 30-year yields.
turns.zh: 我们看到的是一个火热的 CPI 数字，债券收益率开始上升，到一天结束时，从峰值到谷底，我们看到10年期和30年期收益率都有接近25个基点（bps）的波动。

turns.en: So did core weave change the macro regime? Are we moving away from expanding growth and expanding inflation to that of potentially some slowness coming in as everyone has to curtail their expectations?
turns.zh: 所以 CoreWeave 改变了宏观格局（regime）吗？我们是否在从扩张性增长和扩张性通胀转向潜在的某种放缓，因为每个人都不得不削减他们的预期？

turns.en: If that's the story, then the question becomes, are we seeing a rebound in treasury bonds based upon that thesis? Now, look, one day doesn't make a new trend, but the fact that this reversal happened at this inflection point is only stacking intermarket evidence that something meaningful started yesterday, and I'm going to be watching whether or not many of these things follow through.
turns.zh: 如果那是故事，那么问题就变成了：我们是否看到国债基于那个论点的反弹？现在，看，一天不能造就一个新趋势，但这个反转在这个拐点发生的事实，只是在叠加跨市场（intermarket）证据，表明昨天开始了某种有意义的东西，我将密切关注这些东西中的很多是否会跟进。

turns.en: The other important things to highlight is that the December 2027 SOFR contract potentially doubled bottom and started to reverse as the market suddenly started to pull rate hikes off the table in the next year.
turns.zh: 另一个重要的亮点是2027年12月的 SOFR 合约可能双底（double bottom）并开始反转，因为市场突然开始把未来一年的加息从桌面上拿掉。

turns.en: And so this stacked with the fact that we continue to see junk bond credit spreads widening. There's further evidence that there's some sort of a risk-off scare occurring, and potentially treasury bonds may be a defensive asset in this period.
turns.zh: 所以这叠加了我们继续看到垃圾债券信用利差扩大的事实。有进一步的证据表明正在发生某种避险（risk-off）恐慌，国债在这段时期可能是一种防御性资产。

turns.en: While all of that has had an effect on the dollar too, I mean, we've seen pretty much similar moves, but does that change your outlook on anything in terms of the dollar?
turns.zh: 虽然所有这些也对美元有影响，我是说，我们看到了几乎类似的走势，但这改变你对美元的任何展望吗？

turns.en: Well, listen, on that CPI number, the US dollar ripped to a higher high. It printed almost 103 on the upside, but this morning we find ourselves with the dollar pulling back.
turns.zh: 嗯，听着，在那个 CPI 数字上，美元飙升到一个更高的高点。它几乎触及上行的103，但今天早上我们发现美元在回落。

turns.en: It is still a primary bull trend, but we are going to be looking at this from an intermarket perspective. If all the other intermarket signals that we're looking at that we just discussed earlier start to come to fruition, the question is, will it start to pressure US dollar flows?
turns.zh: 它仍然是一个主要的牛市趋势（bull trend），但我们将从跨市场（intermarket）的角度来看这个。如果我们刚才讨论的所有其他跨市场信号都开始实现，问题是，它会开始对美元流动施加压力吗？

turns.en: At this moment, it's very premature to jump to any conclusions. The dollar index could easily absorb a pullback down towards 101, but so long as dips are being bought, I would still consider it technically in a clean bull trend.
turns.zh: 此时此刻，下任何结论都为时过早。美元指数可以轻易吸收一个回落到101附近的回调，但只要低点在被买入，我仍然会认为它在技术上处于一个干净的牛市趋势中。

turns.en: All right, let's start to crude oil because it's been consolidating in a key zone and it seems to be breaking out again, but what are you seeing beneath the headline price?
turns.zh: 好，让我们开始谈原油，因为它一直在一个关键区间盘整，似乎又在突破。但你在表面价格之下看到了什么？

turns.en: Well, I'm actually fascinated by what's happening in crude oil right now because we see structurally strong crude oil markets in Brent and in so many other parts of the oil markets, but the WTI contract remains somewhat in consolidation.
turns.zh: 嗯，我实际上对原油现在正在发生的事情很着迷，因为我们在 Brent 和石油市场的很多其他部分看到结构性强劲的原油市场，但 WTI 合约仍然多少在盘整中。

turns.en: To better understand what is actually happening, you have to actually look at the full term structure on the oil curve. What we're seeing is backwardation flattening.
turns.zh: 要更好地理解实际发生了什么，你必须实际看石油曲线的完整期限结构。我们看到的是现货升水（backwardation）在变平。

turns.en: What's happening here is that the front month oil contract is, let's say, 6% off of its September 15th highs, but yet if you go, let's say, out to April of next year's oil contract over the same days since September 15th, it's up 10% or $10 per barrel.
turns.zh: 这里发生的是，近月（front month）石油合约，比方说，比9月15日的高点低6%，但如果你看，比方说，到明年4月的石油合约，从9月15日以来的同样天数，它涨了10%或每桶10美元。

turns.en: What we continue to see is that oil is under a lot of pressure and that front month contract is not reflecting that. The interesting part is that when you go to the Commitment of Trader Reports, you continue to see that we're at multi-year extremes in terms of gross short positioning in crude oil futures and that may be playing an influence on the price on that front month contract.
turns.zh: 我们继续看到的是，石油承受着很大压力，而近月合约没有反映出这一点。有趣的是，当你去看 Commitment of Traders（交易者持仓）报告时，你继续看到我们在原油期货的总空头头寸方面处于多年极端水平，这可能对那个近月合约的价格产生影响。

turns.en: Clearly, on a geopolitical front, military operations continue to look like they're escalating, not de-escalating. The situation in the Strait of Hormuz looks as spicy as it's been in a long time.
turns.zh: 显然，在地缘政治方面，军事行动继续看起来在升级，而不是降级。霍尔木兹海峡（Strait of Hormuz）的局势看起来和很久以来一样火爆。

turns.en: Really at this moment, the question is, with such depleted inventories, how long can the front month of the WTI contract stay contained the way that it has been over the last three weeks?
turns.zh: 此时此刻，真正的问题是，在库存如此耗尽的情况下，WTI 合约的近月能像过去三周那样保持受控多久？

turns.en: All right. Let's talk about the safe haven asset. Gold still hasn't found its footing and it's trading near a key psychological level of $4,000.
turns.zh: 好。让我们谈谈避险资产。黄金仍然没有站稳，它在交易接近4000美元的关键心理水平附近。

turns.en: Now, where do we go next from here? Gold has consolidated back down to its previous lows, but what is going to be interesting to me is that will we start to see gold respond bullishly to what we just witnessed in the last 24 hours?
turns.zh: 现在，我们从这里往哪里走？黄金已经盘整回它之前的低点，但对我来说有趣的是，我们是否会开始看到黄金对我们刚刚在过去24小时见证的事情做出看涨反应？

turns.en: When we have bond yields start to come off, as bonds start to rally, and if we have growth expectations starting to curtail, inevitably, the market is going to start to price in a Fed that's going to have to be much easier in 2027.
turns.zh: 当我们有债券收益率开始回落，债券开始反弹，如果我们有增长预期开始削减，不可避免地，市场将开始定价一个在2027年将不得不宽松得多的 Fed。

turns.en: Now, if this starts to materialize, the conditions may actually become bullish for gold. Now, we have not seen that reflected in the price yet.
turns.zh: 现在，如果这开始实现，条件实际上可能变得对黄金看涨。但我们还没有看到价格反映出这一点。

turns.en: While we do have in the pre-market here, gold price that is currently rising, but we haven't yet seen any trend line breaks, anything closing above key moving averages.
turns.zh: 虽然我们在盘前这里有黄金价格当前在上升，但我们还没有看到任何趋势线突破，任何收盘在关键均线之上。

turns.en: So while there is a case to be made that gold could potentially establish a bottom here, we haven't yet seen the price starting to show any signs of reflecting that.
turns.zh: 所以虽然有理由认为黄金可能在这里建立底部，但我们还没有看到价格开始显示出反映这一点的任何迹象。

turns.en: And so we're going to continue to watch closely whether the support line holds here. All right. For this week's positioning, Paul Spatrick, we need to talk treasuries.
turns.zh: 所以我们将继续密切关注支撑线是否在这里守住。好。对于本周的持仓，Patrick，我们需要谈谈国债。

turns.en: Now, what has caught your attention in terms of positioning here? Well, there's a lot that stood out for me in this week's caught report, but I wanted to really hone in on these treasury bonds because what we possibly saw was a curve repositioning by traders that were positioned in the steepener.
turns.zh: 现在，什么引起了你的注意在持仓方面？嗯，本周的 COT 报告中有很多突出的东西，但我想真的聚焦这些国债，因为我们可能看到的是交易者在陡化交易（steepener）中的曲线重新定位。

turns.en: What we saw was substantial selling in the five-year treasury futures and substantial buying in the long bond. So let's break it down first.
turns.zh: 我们看到的是5年期国债期货的大幅抛售和长债（long bond）的大幅买入。所以让我们先拆解一下。

turns.en: So the five-year treasury flows saw close to 168,000 contracts swing in a week toward the short side. And at the same time on that long bond, we saw close to net buying of 67,000 contracts.
turns.zh: 所以5年期国债资金流一周内向空头方向摆动了接近168,000份合约。同时在长债上，我们看到接近67,000份合约的净买入。

turns.en: So clearly there was some selling in the shorter duration and buying in the longer term. Is this an unwind of an existing steepener or is this potentially a new flattening exposure?
turns.zh: 所以显然在较短久期有一些抛售，在较长期限有买入。这是现有陡化交易的平仓，还是可能是一个新的变平敞口？

turns.en: Now, I want to just make sure it's clear that there is no easy way to determine whether or not this was an unwind of a steepener because this is aggregate positioning and there is no identifiable pairs trades to be able to match to.
turns.zh: 现在，我想确保清楚的是，没有简单的方法来确定这是否是陡化交易的平仓，因为这是总体持仓，没有可识别的配对交易来匹配。

turns.en: It's simply in an interesting situation where we're seeing bonds moving in opposite directions in the positioning scores. And so it'll be interesting to see whether this trend continues in the weeks to come, especially in light of what we just saw start yesterday.
turns.zh: 这只是一个有趣的情况，我们看到债券在持仓分数上向相反方向移动。所以有趣的是看这种趋势在未来几周是否会继续，尤其是考虑到我们昨天刚刚开始看到的事情。
